generation.path: Authored from specs/T-062-dialect-banks.yaml slices.doteli, which T-062 files as status: conditional pending the native-speaker answers N1, N4, N6, N8, N11 — and as LANGUAGE-level (a doteli row is a translation pair with its standard twin, not a spelling pair). Ships as DATA ONLY: with Policy.includeConditionalTables = false the table cannot fire. The commitment to ship every T-062 doteli row met the safety gate: भया -> भयो is refused and recorded in refusedEntries, so this file carries the two rows that are safe to apply, plus the machine-readable reason the third is not.

refusedEntries.reason: REFUSED BY THE SAFETY GATE, not by review. भयो is a member of the shipped medication-acknowledgement TOKENS (CommandRouter ackTokens, :1528-1529), so this rule maps a form ONTO frozen material. §4.7 forbids that in both directions ('no rule may map a form onto one of these, or away from one of these'), and clause (b) of the losslessness invariant fails concretely: the input भया matches no keyword list, while the output भयो matches the ack token set, so matches(canonical) != matches(original) and the rewrite would be able to turn a non-acknowledgement into an acknowledgement. T-062 files this row as confirmed and it is attested in DialectLexicon.json — the linguistic attestation is not in doubt; the REWRITE is what is unsafe. One defective entry refuses its whole table (§4.3, D-4), so shipping it as an entry would silence the safe रह्याको and भण्याको rows too. It is recorded here and pinned as the failing fixture that proves negationMarkerTouched trips (DialectCanonicalizerTests.testNegationMarkerTouchedRefusesBhayaToBhayo). Any future acceptance of this mapping must come from T-077's re-check against the shipped matchers, never from a table edit.
